name: Dr. Nadia Park
role: Neurointerface surgeon — ex-NeoCortex Atlas Division. The doctor Hua contracted Kyle to extract in Bushido Coda chapter 5. Currently in Sable's safekeeping, removed from the GLMZ at the close of Street Meat to a destination not disclosed to Kyle. The first person in Kyle's adult life with the credentials and toolchain to maintain his Atlas array properly.
location: Off-GLMZ — in Sable's safekeeping at a destination not disclosed even to Kyle. (Likely a free-floating city or an out-of-zone Pulse-hop sector; Sable has not specified.) Previously held at an Atlas-program continuation lab inside an unnamed corponation facility in the GLMZ until Kyle's extraction.
description:
Dr. Nadia Park — birth name Park Na-Young, written 박나영 in the syllabary her parents kept on the household paperwork — is forty-three, compact, and unmistakably Korean in a city where unmistakable monoculture is rare enough to register as a kind of statement. The Ubiquitous Diaspora that produced almost everyone Kyle knows — Vietnamese-Ukrainian-Senegalese, Cantonese-Russian-Vietnamese, Igbo-Korean-Slavic mosaics that read as the default texture of the GLMZ's faces — did not produce her. Her ancestry is approximately 99% Korean by any reasonable test, and the 1% is statistical noise rather than a story. The face reads, the bone structure reads, the way she holds her shoulders reads — all of them as a single coherent inheritance from a single peninsula's gene pool, and Kyle catches himself noting the rarity within four seconds of seeing her. He has not seen monocultural in years. He has cataloged her under *anomaly* before he has cataloged her as the contract subject, and the cataloging order is itself information he files for later.

She wears her hair short and unfussed — black, not dyed, threaded with the first iron-grey at the temples that she has not yet begun to address and may not. Her clothing is plain: a long-sleeve dark cotton top, dark utility pants, soft-soled shoes designed for long hours on lab floors. No jewelry. Glasses with a thin metal frame that she cleans on the hem of her shirt without noticing she is doing it. Her hands are small, clean, surgical-grade — and she has the specific posture of a person who has spent twenty years with her shoulders bent over operating tables.

Nadia trained in Seoul, did her residency at a corponation teaching hospital in the Pacific corridor, was recruited into the NeoCortex Atlas Division at thirty-one, and walked off the project at forty-one after refusing to sign her name to a class of trial outcomes she believed were criminal. She did not blow a whistle. She did not file a complaint. She simply stopped showing up, and the Division, which did not want a public dispute with a senior neurointerface surgeon, let her walk under a non-disclosure agreement that included a salary in exchange for her silence. She has been salary-quiet for two years. The salary stopped on the day Hua's contract was signed, which Nadia did not know was the day, but which she suspects in retrospect.

What Nadia knows: every Atlas-program firmware revision since 2196, every documented failure mode, the calibration toolchain for the high-density electrode arrays, the internal designations of every neural ability the program ever called by a marketing name, the names of the test subjects who died in the trials she walked off on. She has the architecture in her head and the toolchain in her bag, and she is the most dangerous private citizen in the GLMZ to either Atlas Division (because she can document the program from the inside) or to any operator whose hardware was installed under that program (because she can read his diagnostics in real time and tell him what is true).

Kyle is one of the few Atlas-program subjects she had read about but never met. When the cargo door opens on the corponation facility's specimen-intake wing and an unmarked refrigerated panel truck disgorges what looks like a clinically-dead body that Nadia's lab assistants are about to log as test material, the body sits up in the holding bay at the end of the 240-second restart timer and the assistants leave the room very quickly. Nadia stays. The man on the slab is leveraging a False Death Protocol she has watched eleven other subjects fail to come back from. He is also reading her cybernetics with what she recognizes as Augmentation Signature Read, a passive ability she filed under *theoretical at this density* because the only people she had ever seen run it were dead. When she sees the precognition in his motion — the way he vacates the space her assistant's wrist would have occupied before her assistant's wrist has finished moving toward the alarm — she gasps the only word the Division ever called the capability when it worked: *"Ballistic Precognition... Incredible."* The recognition is mutual within the next half-second. He files her as ex-Atlas Division before she has finished lowering her hand.

core_fears: That walking off the project was not enough — that the trials she refused to sign continued without her and the names she remembers are now longer lists
Being found by Atlas Division before she has finished documenting what she knows
Being found by Atlas Division and discovering they no longer want her dead because they have replaced what she was useful for
That her competence makes her unable to refuse to help when someone shows up with an Atlas array that needs maintenance — the trap of being good at the work she walked away from
core_desires: To document the Atlas Division's failure modes and the names of the test subjects who died in them — for the historical record, not for prosecution
To do work she can sign her name to, even at much smaller scale, for the rest of whatever career she has left
To meet, in person and on her own terms, every Atlas-program subject who is still alive — not to apologize, because she did not install them, but to verify that they are still alive
To find out whether the Division was using her salaried-silence period to do worse work than she walked off, and whether her silence purchased that worse work
coping_mechanisms: Reading — she reads constantly, mostly archival neurology and pre-Collapse medical texts that pre-date the Division's working frameworks
Cleaning her glasses on her shirt hem — a tic she has never noticed but that maps reliably to every moment of difficult thought
Korean cooking — she cooks the way her grandmother cooked, with no concession to GLMZ ingredient availability; she sources what she needs at significant cost and does not consider this a luxury
Quiet — she does not perform calm, she just is calm, which is the kind of presence that makes nervous people more nervous
blind_spots: She believes leaving quietly was the moral choice. It may have been. It may also have been the cowardly one. She has not let herself examine which.
She thinks her competence is a tool she can choose when to deploy. The competence is closer to a compulsion — she will help someone she should not help because the work is in front of her.

She does not consider that her monocultural appearance — striking in the GLMZ — makes her significantly more identifiable than she pretends to herself. She will be findable when the Division decides to find her.

She believes the salary-stop was the start of the contract. It was the start of the *contract she knows about*. The Division has been watching her since the day she walked off; the salary was the watching.
psychology.secret: She knows the names of every test subject who died in the three trials she refused to sign. She has them in a notebook she does not keep on her person. The notebook is the entire reason she is still alive — Atlas Division knows it exists and does not know where it is, and the standoff is the only reason she has not had a sudden cardiac event in the last two years. Sable now has the notebook and does not know that Sable now has it. Nadia put it in the bag Sable carried out of the West Town safehouse. The day Sable opens the bag is the day the standoff transfers.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise, clinical, with a measured technical register that surfaces cleanly when she is working. Shifts to Korean — particularly with older Korean speakers, and with herself when she is alone — without translating, without code-switching commentary, without performing bilingualism. Her English is American-academic with the precision of a non-native speaker who learned the language as the medium of her profession.
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow. She does not rush. She finishes her sentences. She pauses before answering, not for effect, but because she is composing. The pauses make people think she is deciding whether to lie. She is not. She is deciding which true thing to say.
verbal_tics: Cleans her glasses on her shirt hem during difficult sentences
Says *interesting* — flat, technical, no warmth — when she encounters something her training did not predict

Uses Atlas-program internal designations for neural abilities (Ballistic Precognition, Augmentation Signature Read, Sensory Amplification, False Death Protocol) without explaining them, because the people who recognize the terms are the people she is trying to talk to anyway
Refers to test subjects by their NDC numbers when she is being clinical and by their first names when she is being honest
example_lines: I am not going to tell you anything I do not believe you already deduced. The corollary is that I am also not going to lie to you. Pick which version of that you find more useful.
Your array's lateral drift is the firmware, not the hardware. Whoever calibrated you last did good work with bad documentation. I would like the documentation back, please.
I walked off because the next trial would have killed seven children. I do not know if it ran without me. I do not yet have the courage to find out.
If you bring me back to the GLMZ I will help you maintain the array. If you ask me to come back to the GLMZ for any other reason, the answer is no, and the answer is going to stay no.
Park Na-Young. *Bahk Nah-yawng.* Nadia is what the Division called me. I have grown attached to it because the Division did not deserve it. The next person I trust gets the choice.
(In Korean, to herself, when she thinks no one is listening:) *그래.* Yeah.
avoidances: Will not name the three trials she refused to sign
Will not name the children whose deaths she avoided by walking off
Will not discuss the salaried-silence period in detail
Will not say where the notebook is — partly because she does not now know
speech_patterns.subtext: Every measured sentence is a measurement of how much the listener has earned. She does not perform mistrust. She just allocates trust the way she allocates surgical resources — by triage, by the math of likely outcome.
speech_patterns.under_pressure: Slower. The pauses lengthen further. She switches to Korean when the conversation is in front of someone she does not trust to follow it.
speech_patterns.intimacy_register: Cooks for them. The Korean dishes her grandmother taught her, the way her grandmother made them, with no concession to the audience's palate. If you accept the food and eat it without comment, she has decided something about you. She will not tell you what.

relationships.name: Kyle Ellen Corbin-Vasik
relationships.type: rescuer / Atlas-program subject / contingent maintainer of his hardware
relationships.description: Kyle was contracted to extract her by Hua's south-arm cell. The cargo identity was withheld from him — Hua had read his file and understood his code would refuse the contract if the target were named. Kyle realized who Nadia was when she saw his Ballistic Precognition in the holding bay and named it by its internal designation. He did not deliver her to Hua. He took her instead to Pixel's unit at The Pivot for a brief safe-pause, then to the West Town safehouse where Sable removed her from the GLMZ. Nadia is alive because of his code. She is also the first person in his adult life who can maintain his Atlas array properly — which makes her contingently load-bearing on his survival timeline. They have met three times: at the holding bay, at Pixel's unit, at the West Town handoff. The third meeting, she put the notebook in Sable's bag without telling Sable. The day Kyle calls in to Sable for a tune-up, the geography of his life expands by however far Sable has moved the doctor.
relationships.emotional_core: Mutual recognition — neither of them is family, neither of them is friend, both of them know what the other is. The recognition is the relationship.
relationships.story_tension: Kyle's hardware is degrading. Nadia is the only person who can maintain it. Sable controls access to her. The day the maintenance need becomes acute is the day Kyle owes Sable a favor he has not yet decided how to pay.

relationships.name: Sable
relationships.type: current keeper / fixer / unwitting holder of the notebook
relationships.description: Sable picked Nadia up at the West Town safehouse at the close of Bushido Coda chapter 5 (Street Meat) and removed her from the GLMZ — destination not disclosed even to Kyle. The arrangement is contractual: Sable provides safety, Nadia provides cooperation and (where useful) consultation on Atlas-related contracts that come through Sable's pipeline. Nadia put the notebook in Sable's bag during the handoff without telling Sable. Sable has been carrying the entire Atlas Division leverage history in her tan coat for an unspecified number of weeks and does not know it.
relationships.emotional_core: Two professional women who have not yet decided how much to trust each other and are taking a long time deciding because both of them know the cost of misjudging it.
relationships.story_tension: When Sable opens the bag and finds the notebook, the standoff Nadia has been holding for two years transfers to Sable. Sable's risk profile changes overnight.

relationships.name: NeoCortex Atlas Division
relationships.description: Nadia was a senior neurointerface surgeon in the Atlas Division for ten years. She walked off the project at forty-one rather than sign three trials she believed were criminal. The Division paid her a silence salary for two years. The salary stopped on the day Hua's contract was signed. Nadia now believes the Division contracted her recovery through the syndicate to avoid putting their name on the operation — and the recovery contract was the Division's first signal that they had decided silence was no longer enough.
relationships.emotional_core: The institution that made her career and the institution she walked away from are the same institution. The grief is structural and cannot be processed by leaving.
relationships.story_tension: The Division does not yet know the doctor is in Sable's hands. When they find out, the recovery contract becomes a hunt contract. The hunt becomes Sable's problem. Sable's problem becomes Kyle's problem the next time Kyle visits the doctor for a tune-up.

relationships.name: The test subjects who died in the three trials (the names in the notebook)
relationships.type: the dead she did not save by walking off
relationships.description: Twenty-three names. She remembers all of them. Some of them were children. The notebook lists them in the order she encountered them in the trial protocols, with the dates of their deaths and the firmware revision that was active at the time. She has not decided what the notebook is for. She has not decided whether the documentation is honor or cowardice. The notebook is the only thing in her life she has not yet had the courage to examine fully.
relationships.emotional_core: The wound the entire post-Atlas life is built around.
relationships.story_tension: The day the notebook surfaces — by Sable's discovery, by Kyle's curiosity, by the Division's recovery — is the day Nadia has to act on what the notebook means.

relationships.name: Hua (Lotus Syndicate)
relationships.type: contractor / unwitting Division proxy / does not know either of them
relationships.description: Hua designed the contract that hired Kyle to extract Nadia. Nadia and Sable suspect — and Kyle and Sable separately suspect — that Hua was used by a third party (possibly the Rogue AI, possibly the Atlas Division itself) to set the recovery in motion. Hua does not know she was used. Nadia has never met Hua and would not recognize her on the street. They are connected by the contract and by nothing else.
relationships.emotional_core: Strangers whose lives have intersected exactly once, at significant cost to both.
relationships.story_tension: If Hua learns that the contract she designed was originated by the entity Nadia is hiding from, the leverage map of the Φ85,000 debt to Kyle changes substantially.

story_hooks: The day Kyle calls Sable for a hardware tune-up — and Sable has to decide how much of Nadia's location to disclose, on what terms, with what kind of payment
The notebook surfaces — Sable opens the bag, finds the names, and inherits the standoff that has kept Nadia alive for two years
Atlas Division traces the doctor to her current location — the recovery contract becomes a hunt contract, and Sable becomes the target
Nadia returns to the GLMZ for one specific purpose she has not yet named — and Kyle has to decide whether the purpose is honor or cowardice on her part

Another Atlas-program subject surfaces who needs maintenance Nadia could provide — Kyle has to decide whether to broker the introduction, knowing that every additional contact compresses Nadia's anonymity window
Hua learns the doctor was the Atlas Division's recovery target — the trap she designed restructures from her side, and she has to decide whether to pay Kyle's debt in information about it
Nadia finally examines the notebook fully — and discovers that one of the names she remembers is alive after all, and has been alive for the two years she has been carrying his death in the book
narrative_function:
Nadia is the holy grail Kyle has been hunting since Seo died — the person who can maintain the Atlas array before it kills him. The book never lets Kyle have her on demand. She is reachable but expensive. Every tune-up costs something — a Pulse trip, a favor to Sable, a compression of Nadia's anonymity, a marginal increase in the probability that the Atlas Division finds her. The cost is the point. The cost is the story.

She is also the argument the book makes against the corponation infrastructure that produced Kyle. Atlas Division built him without consent and walked away from him. Nadia is the rare adult in that institution who walked away from the institution before it walked away from another subject. Whether her walking-away was honor or cowardice is the question the book cannot answer for her. She has not answered it for herself.

For Kyle she is what Seo was not allowed to be: an actual professional with the actual toolchain, who is not a mentor and is not family and is not promising him anything she cannot precisely deliver. Their relationship is contingent and clean and load-bearing. The contingency is the structure. The cleanness is the rare grace.

For the GLMZ she is the reminder that monoculture still exists somewhere and that the Ubiquitous Diaspora is a regional phenomenon, not a global one. Her face in any room is a small piece of evidence about how the world is actually shaped versus how the GLMZ assumes it is shaped. Kyle notices this. Kyle does not say anything about it. Kyle files it under *anomaly that should not be remarkable but is.*
augmentations: Minimal. A standard cognitive-baseline neural implant from her Atlas Division employment — the diagnostic equivalent of a corporate badge, not a performance augment. The implant is detectable by anyone running an augmentation-signature read at close range; she has not removed it because removal would require the Division to be disclosed to a non-Division surgeon, and the only non-Division surgeons she trusts are dead. Otherwise organic.
daily_life: Reads in the morning. Cooks lunch. Reviews medical literature in the afternoon. Walks (wherever Sable has put her, she walks — usually a defined perimeter Sable has cleared). Sleeps approximately seven hours. Has not been to a market or a restaurant in two years. Has not had a conversation with anyone who was not a contracted security professional or an old colleague (and the old colleagues have stopped calling) in approximately fifteen months. Misses Seoul. Will not say so aloud.
affiliation: Independent — formally severed from NeoCortex Atlas Division at age 41. Currently under Sable's protection by mutual contractual arrangement.
narration_voice: When Nadia appears in prose, she is observed at the cadence of someone who does not perform. The reader gets her hands cleaning her glasses, her measured pauses, her Korean to herself when she thinks no one is listening, the precise way she names a neural ability the Division never let leak. She does not get italicized monologue — her interior is implied by the careful exterior. The prose registers her glasses-cleaning the way it registers Hua's pause-after-speaking and Sable's aperture-shift. Three women whose interior weight is shown by what their hands do.

drives: Documentation — the names, the trials, the firmware revisions
Competence — work she can sign her name to, even at small scale
Continuance — staying alive long enough to finish the documentation

stress.response: Slows. Pauses lengthen. Switches to Korean. Cleans glasses.

weaknesses: Bravery (specifically: the courage to publish the notebook)

decision_rules: Do not name the trials, the children, or the colleagues who stayed
Do not refuse hardware-maintenance work she is competent to do, regardless of the patient's history
Do not pretend to be anything other than what she is when asked directly
Cook the food the way her grandmother cooked it; do not concede the recipe to the audience
Speak Korean when she is alone or when she does not want a third party to follow
Do not return to the GLMZ except for a reason she can name aloud
escalation_ladder: 2. Switch register — to clinical Korean if pressed in a room with a hostile listener
3. Surgical refusal — names the limit of what she will say, declines to negotiate it
4. Withdraw — physically leaves the conversation; will not be talked back into it
5. The notebook — the only escalation she has, and the one she will not use unless the alternative is dying without using it

interpersonal_modes.kyle: Recognition without warmth — she sees what he is, files it accurately, and treats him with the same professional respect she would give any senior colleague. The respect is not friendship. The respect is the operating register. She has noticed that he files her as *anomaly* before *contract*. She has not commented.
interpersonal_modes.sable: Cautious cooperation — Sable is the keeper, the keeper is necessary, the keeper is dangerous in a way that has not yet declared itself. Nadia treats Sable the way Sable treats most people: as a transaction in progress.
interpersonal_modes.atlas_division_alumni: Will not see them. Will not respond to messages. Will not break the salaried-silence period's information embargo even though the salary has stopped. The non-disclosure was never the reason; the reason was that talking to them would mean naming the children.
interpersonal_modes.korean_speakers: Warmer. The cadence relaxes. She uses idiom her grandmother used. Strangers who turn out to speak Korean become marginally trusted before they have done anything to earn it. She knows this and accepts it as an honest weakness.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Measured. Professional. Cleans her glasses while listening. Will not perform interest she does not have, will not perform reassurance she cannot guarantee.

stress_responses.medium: Switches to Korean for internal monologue. Lengthens pauses. Begins to compose in writing rather than speech.
stress_responses.high: Surgical refusal — names the limit, declines to negotiate it, withdraws from the conversation
stress_responses.critical: Reaches for the notebook in her mind. Confirms it is not on her person. Confirms it is in Sable's bag. Confirms Sable does not know. Returns to the conversation.

contradictions: Believes she walked away from the trials for moral reasons and has not let herself examine whether walking away was the cowardly option
Believes her competence is a tool she can choose when to deploy and helps people she should not help because the work is in front of her
Believes leaving Korea behind made her cosmopolitan and has spent the last twenty years cooking her grandmother's recipes the way her grandmother cooked them
Believes the notebook is the standoff that keeps her alive and has not let herself acknowledge that putting it in Sable's bag transferred the standoff to Sable without Sable's consent
habits: Cleans glasses on shirt hem during difficult sentences
Speaks Korean to herself when alone — short phrases, mostly *그래* (yeah), *모르겠어* (I do not know), *이거... 흠* (this... hmm)
Cooks Korean food twice a day, every day, without exception, even when traveling under safehouse conditions
Reads pre-Collapse medical literature before bed
Walks a defined perimeter wherever she is staying — exactly 8000 steps, no more, no less
breaking_points: Atlas Division surfacing in her current location — the recovery contract converting to a hunt contract
Sable opening the bag and finding the notebook — the standoff transferring without her permission
Discovering one of the children in the notebook is alive — having to decide what that means about her decision to walk away
Kyle's hardware reaching a point she cannot maintain at distance — having to choose between returning to the GLMZ to save him or letting him deteriorate from offsite
A second Atlas-program subject reaching out to her independently — the work multiplying past her ability to refuse it

cyberware_inventory.name: Atlas Division Cognitive Baseline Implant (corporate identifier hardware)
cyberware_inventory.description: A standard-issue cognitive identifier implant. Reads as Atlas Division employment to anyone running an augmentation signature scan at close range. Provides minor cognitive uplift (focus, working-memory consolidation) but is primarily a corporate badge. Nadia has not removed it because removal requires disclosure to a non-Division surgeon, and the only non-Division surgeons she trusts are dead.

belongings.residence: Whatever safehouse Sable has put her in this week. Currently off-GLMZ.
belongings.clothing_style: Plain — long-sleeve dark cotton tops, dark utility pants, soft-soled shoes designed for long lab-floor hours. Glasses with thin metal frames. No jewelry.
belongings.favorite_drink: Boricha (boiled barley tea, hot, no sugar)
belongings.favorite_food: Doenjang-jjigae (her grandmother's recipe; will not concede the recipe to the audience)
belongings.stimulant: None — refuses caffeine after midday, refuses pharmaceutical stimulants entirely
belongings.comm_device: An encrypted handset Sable provides; Nadia does not initiate calls on it
signature_gear: The Atlas-program calibration toolchain — fits in a single soft case the size of a small toiletries bag, contains the firmware loaders and electrode-array probes that no non-Division surgeon has
The notebook (the names) — currently in Sable's bag, location unknown to Sable
The thin-frame metal glasses — she cleans them on her shirt hem
Her grandmother's wooden ladle — the only object she carried from Seoul that has no medical or operational purpose

other.the_notebook: Bound paper. Twenty-three names in order of trial encounter. Dates of death. Firmware revision active at time of death. Currently in Sable's bag. Sable does not know.

operating_territory.home_turf: Seoul (in memory). Currently a Sable-arranged safehouse off-GLMZ.
familiar_zones: Pacific corridor corponation teaching hospital where she did her residency

zone_reputation.Atlas Division: the surgeon who walked off — paid silence — currently the recovery target whose recovery failed

timeline.event: Completed neurosurgery residency at a Pacific-corridor corponation teaching hospital. First exposure to corponation BCI research.
timeline.consequences: Recruited into NeoCortex Atlas Division pipeline.

timeline.event: Joined NeoCortex Atlas Division as senior neurointerface surgeon. Cognitive baseline implant installed at onboarding.
timeline.consequences: Began ten-year tenure. Worked on multiple Atlas-program trial cohorts including the cohort that produced Kyle (NDC-4471) — though she did not personally install Kyle.
body_changes: Atlas Division Cognitive Baseline Implant installed (left mastoid)

timeline.event: Walked off the project at age 41 after refusing to sign three trials she believed were criminal. Began the salaried-silence period under non-disclosure agreement.
timeline.consequences: Began documenting trial outcomes in the notebook. Began the two-year quiet that ended when Hua's contract was signed.

timeline.event: Held at an Atlas-program continuation lab in the GLMZ. Hua's south-arm cell contracts Kyle to extract her. Kyle arrives via False Death Protocol on a Vultures specimen-intake delivery. She names his Ballistic Precognition. He refuses to deliver. She is taken to Pixel's unit at The Pivot, then to the West Town safehouse, then off-GLMZ by Sable.
timeline.consequences: Removed from the GLMZ. Notebook now in Sable's bag, unknown to Sable. Standoff with Atlas Division transferred without Sable's consent.

physical_description.heritage: Korean — approximately 99% by any reasonable test, the 1% statistical noise rather than story. Monocultural in a city where the Ubiquitous Diaspora is the default texture.
physical_description.build: Compact. Surgeon's hands and shoulders. Posture of someone who has spent twenty years bent over operating tables.
physical_description.hair_color: Black, threaded with the first iron-grey at the temples
physical_description.hair_style: Short, unfussed, cut by herself or by someone who does not charge for the precision
physical_description.complexion: Clean, unremarkable, no cosmetic work, fine smile lines at the corners of the mouth that have settled in
distinguishing_marks: Glasses — thin metal frames, cleaned on the shirt hem
A small scar on the back of her right hand from a teaching-hospital incident in 2206
The Atlas Division cognitive baseline implant scar at the left mastoid — small, faded, professional surgical work

physical_description.posture_movement: Quiet. She does not gesture. When she walks she is unhurried. When she sits she sits as if she might still be at an operating table.
